narrative.overview: A clear daylight storefront: upright lettering, broad blue fields and useful yellow actions. Outdoors photography gives the site a place to breathe; flat product illustrations make the fictional merchandise easy to inspect. The identity is provisional and can evolve with actual merchant use.
keyCharacteristics: Cool, light grounds rather than aged-paper nostalgia.
Plain shopping controls and a compact, bold wordmark.
Photography and product art, not decorative badges or invented social proof.

rules.name: The Daylight Rule
rules.body: Keep product inspection on light surfaces and use dark blue ink for the reading layer.

rules.name: The Upright Rule
rules.body: Let scale and wording carry hierarchy, rather than tiny tracked labels above headings.

dos: Do use real product imagery or explicitly labeled illustrative designs.
Do keep every state usable without motion.
Do keep the demo banner concise and the detailed instructions on their own route.
donts: Don't add faux park insignia, invented reviews or unsupported environmental claims.
Don't use prices or availability from the brand seed as storefront authority.
